messages:
ellie.m: Heads-up: noticed a subtle bug with our Android sample app where Authorization header ends up stale for a short window when using an application interceptor + Authenticator + coroutines. Repro and notes below.

ellie.m: Environment: emulator API 31, okhttp 4.10, retrofit 2.9, Kotlin coroutines. Pattern: app sets Authorization via an application interceptor reading from TokenStore; on 401 Authenticator triggers a blocking refresh and returns new request. Sometimes a following request immediately after refresh still gets old token header.

omar.f: That sounds like a read-after-write race on TokenStore. Are you atomically updating the token or is the interceptor reading a cached field that isn't volatile?

ellie.m: TokenStore is a simple object with a var token: String and synchronized update in refresh. Interceptor reads token without synchronization. We assumed volatile var would be enough but Kotlin "var" isn't volatile by default.

omar.f: Right. With multiple threads the interceptor may read a stale value. Two paths: either make token volatile (AtomicReference) or ensure interceptor reads via a threadsafe getter. Also Authenticator runs on OkHttp's internal thread pool so memory visibility matters.

ryan.l: Another nuance: application interceptors run before network interceptors and can be invoked on different threads. If Authenticator updates TokenStore after returning new request, there can be a tiny window where the next new request picks up an old token. We solved this in server-sdk by having Authenticator publish the new token before returning, and using an AtomicReference with compareAndSet to avoid lost updates.

ellie.m: We tried AtomicReference and the problem reduced but we still saw edge cases in low-RAM emulator under stress. We also have a pattern where interceptor reads token once at request start then reuses it for the whole chain — any better idea?

omar.f: Best practice for Android SDK: (1) store token in AtomicReference or volatile var, (2) synchronize refresh so only one refresh happens (singleflight), (3) make interceptor fetch token at request time from the threadsafe accessor (not cache it across requests).

ryan.l: Also consider using an Authentication interceptor that adds header at the network level rather than application level if you need header to be current at time of network dispatch. But beware network interceptors see different state (they run later) and they can see connection-specific behaviors.

ellie.m: Good call. We also found that use of .addHeader vs .header in building requests caused duplicate header values in some flows when interceptor re-ran. Switched to .header to overwrite, fixed duplicates.

omar.f: For docs: add a small checklist under "Android SDK: Auth and retries" — AtomicReference token, serialize refresh, avoid caching token in interceptors, use .header to overwrite, and sample code for a replayable RequestBody for uploads.

sdk-bot: created issue #4126: "android-sdk: Authenticator/Interceptor race -> stale header" assigned to @omar.f

ellie.m: Thanks — I'll prototype a tiny TokenProvider with AtomicReference + mutex, update sample app, and run emulator matrix across API 28/29/31. Will paste results here.

ryan.l: One more gotcha: if you use WorkManager or background threads to enqueue requests, make sure the token provider is initialized before workers start. We had intermittent NPEs when provider lazily created under concurrency.

ellie.m: Noted. Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with PR and sample changes.
